title: Staggered cutover signal cadence and rollback criteria for runtime/console/api
creator: Asha Patel
description: Establish a standardized cadence of cutover signals, traffic ramps, and explicit rollback criteria to coordinate staggered rollouts across Runtime, Console, and API. The goal is to minimize customer downtime, reduce blast radius, and provide clear ownership and communication protocols during multi-surface launches.
acceptance_criteria: A single Cutover Playbook template exists in Confluence with signal definitions (GO / CAUTION / STOP) and step-by-step actions for each signal
Automated Slack channel alerts and PagerDuty runbook links trigger on pre-defined metric thresholds during canary and ramp phases
Rollback criteria documented and automated health checks wired into the deployment pipeline (SLO-based gating)
Cross-team run-of-show created and validated with runtime, console, api, infra, security, and support owners
Capacity reservation and regional fallback knobs included with owner/time-to-restore estimates
notes: Trade-offs: tighter SLO gates reduce risk but increase rollout time and coordination overhead.
Decision: adopt three-stage signal model (Green/Amber/Red) mapped to percent-of-traffic ramps (0/10/50/100) with explicit wait windows and automated metric checks.
We will pilot with runtime-1.22 feature flags and a Console UI tweak in Cycle 2026-W11 before wider rollout.
Rollback paths considered: instant rollback to previous runtime version, progressive abort of traffic by region, emergency mitigation script to disable new endpoints.
